sourceFacts: Spastic diplegia predominantly affects the legs.
Hemiplegia affects one side; quadriplegia affects all four limbs and may include the trunk and face.
prompt:
Create a polished original medical teaching illustration in landscape 3:2 format. Use the attached MD3 original solely as a style reference: warm watercolour/gouache on an ivory paper background, delicate ink contours, calm navy labels, muted ochre/peach/teal colours, generous whitespace and clear flat anatomical shapes. Anatomical clarity before decoration. Never photorealistic skin, glossy blood, wet flesh, fat lobules, scary faces, chunky 3D tissue blocks, or a fake scan. Only exact requested labels, clean legible short text. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No watermark, logos or attribution in the pixels. Compose an entirely new subject from the clinical specification, not the scalp content in the reference.

Three modest, flat front-facing CHILD BODY MAPS in plain t-shirt and leggings, neutral stance, no actual diagnostic posture. Same size. Left heading 'Diplegia': both legs strongly teal highlighted, arms plain; bottom 'Legs more affected'. Middle 'Hemiplegia': viewer's RIGHT arm and RIGHT leg highlighted ochre, opposite side plain; bottom 'One side affected'. Right 'Quadriplegia': BOTH arms and BOTH legs highlighted muted teal, trunk a lighter wash; bottom 'All four limbs affected'. Title 'Spastic cerebral palsy: distribution'. Small bottom note 'Body maps show distribution, not functional ability'. No chair or walking prediction, no smile/frown severity judgment, no spinal lesion.
